explanation: Consumption was abruptly elevated (+50.2% above expected) for 2 hour(s). Observed: 77 L vs Expected: 52 L in Administration.
possible_causes: Fixture issue, one-time maintenance flushing, lab discharge, irrigation valve burst, or meter surge.
recommended_action: Verify meter reading stability, inspect restrooms and immediate utility lines for active leaks or open taps.
possible_interpretation: Fixture issue, one-time maintenance flushing, lab discharge, irrigation valve burst, or meter surge.
uncertainty_statement: Potential abnormal usage identified from aggregate meter data. This is NOT a confirmed physical leak and requires human on-site verification before any maintenance action.
recommendation:
Recommended Operational Action: Decision Support & Human Verification Protocol
- Evidence [Decision Support & Human Verification Protocol] (water_ops_guidance.md): AquaGuard AI alerts are operational decision-support indicators derived from statistical and machine learning evaluation of aggregate consumption telemetry. Anomaly detection does NOT constitute physical confirmation of a pipe rupture or leak. Human facility staff must physically inspect the target site, cross-reference work logs, and confirm physical symptoms prior to taking invasive corrective actions. Autonomous water shutoff is strictly prohibited.
- Evidence [Sustainable Campus Water Management (SDG 6)] (water_ops_guidance.md): Aligning campus infrastructure with UN Sustainable Development Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) involves continuous water auditing, sub-metering high-draw facilities (laboratories, kitchens, athletic centers), installing low-flow aerators, harvesting rainwater for landscape irrigation, and fostering student water conservation awareness.
